title: Q3 playbook: private instance offramp and re-onramp strategy (safety + OKR traceability)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: define a quarterly playbook for safe offboarding (temporary or permanent) of customer private instances and a repeatable re-onramp process. This ticket captures scope for runbooks, automation, acceptance criteria, and OKR-level traceability so teams can measure risk reduction across Q3. Rationale: as we scale Private deployments, we need standardized, low-risk ways to retire, pause, or reconfigure tenant instances (for compliance, underutilization, or customer request) while ensuring we can re-onramp with preserved data/config and within SLA constraints. Scope includes: operator-run offramp steps, automated pre-checks, data export/import validation, rollback windows, customer communication templates, billing/commit reconciliation, and metrics to demonstrate reduced mean time to restore (MTTR) and reduced incident impact. Out of scope: deep data migration between major schema versions (handled by migration initiative) and long-term archival policies beyond 1 year.

acceptance_criteria: Operator can execute an offramp runbook that creates a verified snapshot and isolates network in < 30 minutes for tenants < 1TB (measured in staging).
Automated pre-checks run and surface blocking issues (schema mismatch, pending backups, active long-running jobs) with actionable errors shown in Console.
Customer-facing termination email template and portal UI flow updated; Support playbook exists and is linked from runbook.
Re-onramp restores snapshot and associated config with data integrity checks passing (hashes) and service health green within configured restore-window (SLO: 2 hours for <1TB).
Billing system marks tenant as paused and prevents new charges during offramp; commit reconciliation reported to finance.
GDPR/region-specific export step present and logged for EU tenants; audit entry created for every offramp/re-onramp event.
Operational runbook includes rollback steps and an objective metric dashboard (MTTR, % successful re-onramps) visible in Console by release.
